verdict: The metrics are computed correctly. I found no blocker or major defects. Every TrackEval setting I was asked to check is correct: GT folder, seqmaps, BENCHMARK/SPLIT, DO_PREPROC, pedestrian class, and Count added automatically. The numpy shim is functionally correct. The 7 Hz benchmark (MOT17sub7-train) has correct seqinfo and correctly renumbered GT. ids_per_gt and merged_ids are computed as documented. My own scorer does not use TrackEval. On 11 run/sequence cases it reproduces per_sequence_metrics.csv exactly: MOTA, IDF1, HOTA, DetA and AssA, the count fields, ids_per_gt and merged_ids (231 values, difference at most 1e-12). Counting the detector P/R directly from the detection caches matches all 14 detector x sequence rows. There are two minor provenance/documentation defects: run_partD.sh does not include the oracle runs, and the shim record overstates what was patched. The observations below are definitional caveats the paper should state.

defects.issue: run_partD.sh does not produce the oracle runs. 10 of the 48 combined rows (oracle__bytetrack_phase2, oracle__workid_phase2, and its _offline, _uidonly and _offline_uidonly variants, at native and 7 Hz) come from tracker runs started by hand, outside the documented pipeline. One of them predates the committed tooling.

The other oracle runs started 19:09:37, 19:11:49 and 19:12:00, all before run_partD.sh began (19:37, logs/run_partD.out). logs/ has no track_oracle_bytetrack_phase2_native.log. The oracle logs that do exist use a different tag format (no feed suffix). The numbers themselves are correct: I re-ran all four oracle runs with the current mot17_track.py (using --smoke-dir into scratch), and all 42 output files (bytetrack, workid and workid_offline, native and 7 Hz, 7 sequences each) are byte-identical to data/revision_r1_cache/partD/trackers/... .

defects.issue: The numpy-shim provenance record and the docstring say three aliases were restored. Under NumPy 2.5.4 only np.float and np.int are patched; np.bool already exists (it is np.bool_, re-added in NumPy 2.0).
defects.evidence: mot17_eval.py:17-19 (docstring: 'The three names are restored as aliases of the builtins'). mot17_eval.py:197 hard-codes "numpy_alias_shim": ["float", "int", "bool"] into trackeval_versions.json. Checked in .venv-eval: before the shim, hasattr(np,'float')=False, hasattr(np,'int')=False, hasattr(np,'bool')=True and np.bool is np.bool_, so the guard at mot17_eval.py:33-35 skips 'bool'. No numeric effect: dtype=np.bool_ equals dtype=bool, and every other np.* name used by TrackEval exists in numpy 2.5.4 (the only miss is 'loadtext', and it appears only in a docstring).
defects.fix: Record the aliases actually set, e.g. patched = [a for a,_ in ALIASES if not hasattr(np, a)] computed before setattr, and write that list. Reword the docstring: np.float and np.int were removed in NumPy 1.24; np.bool exists again since NumPy 2.0 as np.bool_.

observations: Matching rule for ids_per_gt / merged_ids. id_counts (mot17_eval.py:127-129) runs the Hungarian on raw IoU and then keeps pairs >= 0.5; TrackEval zeroes sub-threshold IoU before assigning. The difference is at most 0.011 ids/gt and at most 3 merged IDs on any combined row (e.g. coco__bytetrack_phase2 2.3537 vs 2.3648, merged 167 vs 168). Using CLEAR's own continuity-preferring matches instead lowers merged_ids by up to about 22% on detector-fed runs: coco__bytetrack_phase2 167 to 131, coco__botsort_reid 188 to 150, coco__workid_phase2__feedall 202 to 170. ids/gt drops by about 0.04-0.13, oracle rows change by 2 at most, and the tracker ordering stays the same. The paper should state the per-frame rule exactly.

merged_ids is an absolute count, and it reads very differently once normalised by matched predicted IDs. coco: ByteTrack 167/691 = 24.2% vs Work ID uid-only 171/344 = 49.7%. Oracle, native: ByteTrack 87/549 = 15.8% vs Work ID uid-only 138/375 = 36.8%. Reporting the fraction makes the identity-merge failure visible, where the raw counts (167 vs 171) hide it.

ids_per_gt averages only over GT identities matched at least once. That is 393 of 546 for coco ByteTrack, 253 for grouped and 539 for the oracle, so comparisons across detectors are conditional on detection. Averaged over all 546 identities, coco ByteTrack gives 1.69 rather than 2.35.
The 7 Hz rows score 541 GT identities and 1,541 frames: 5 of the 546 identities appear only in dropped frames. The text should not quote 546 for the 7 Hz rows.

In the detections_conf035 rows only CLR_Pr and CLR_Re (with TP/FP/FN) mean anything. Their HOTA, IDF1, IDSW (47,951) and ids_per_gt (117) are artefacts of one-box tracks and should be kept out of the tables. The precision is MOT17-protocol precision: boxes on static persons, reflections, distractors and persons on vehicles count as neither TP nor FP. coco loses 1,717 of 55,638 boxes this way (P 89.69, or 86.92 if those counted as FP); grouped loses 108 of 24,342 (91.38 vs 90.97).

The main workid_phase2 rows include the probation provisional IDs (>= 1,000,000). Their IDSW and ids/gt are therefore dominated by the switch from probation to uid: coco IDSW 1,048 vs 312 for uid-only, ids/gt 3.39 vs 1.78. The uid-only variant drops the probation boxes, so its DetA is lower (33.9 to 33.2). The paper must name the variant it reports.

CPU ms/frame is wall-clock time (perf_counter) around the tracker call (mot17_track.py:140-151, 177-179, 194-195). It was measured while the two streams ran concurrently (run_partD.sh:45-49) at different thread counts (phase2 1, BoT-SORT 2, StrongSORT/Deep OC-SORT 3), with a GPU job also running. The same ByteTrack calls on the same boxes measured 1.39 vs 1.80 ms/frame for coco and 0.94 vs 1.22 for grouped (ByteTrack run vs inside the Work ID run). My re-run of oracle ByteTrack on MOT17-02 gave 3.1 ms/frame against the recorded 4.65. The numbers hold at order of magnitude (ByteTrack about 1-3 ms, BoT-SORT about 27 ms, StrongSORT/Deep OC-SORT 66-136 ms) but not at 2 decimals. BoT-SORT's ReID features come from the cached detector pass and are excluded; OSNet inference inside StrongSORT/Deep OC-SORT is included. Work ID overhead should be quoted as the identity-layer time (0.89 ms/frame on coco), not as the difference between totals.

In the oracle runs, LocA 99.98 / MOTP < 100 and the single FP on 7 Hz MOT17-10 are genuine CLEAR/HOTA continuity effects (a match is kept to the previous ID's box when IoU >= 0.5), not data errors. My independent code reproduces FP = 1.
The 'Error importing BURST ... pycocotools' line in logs/eval.log is harmless; the BURST dataset is not used.

verdict: The numbers are right, but they can mislead. I found no code bug that changes any reported value. Detector P/R, six reference TrackEval runs, the oracle ByteTrack outputs (byte-identical) and the Work ID uid counts all reproduce independently. Three things could mislead a reader of combined_metrics.csv. (1) MAJOR: there is no probation-matched control for Work ID. Compared with ByteTrack that has the same first-2-appearances drop, the identity layer lowers HOTA, AssA and IDF1 in all six conditions. About a third to a half of the apparent drop in IDs/GT and IDSW comes from dropping probation boxes. (2) The ranking against BoT-SORT comes from the 0.35 input filter, not from association: on equal input ByteTrack ties or beats BoT-SORT. (3) CPU ms/frame is not comparable across trackers: thread counts and load differ, boxmot embeds boxes it then throws away, and BoT-SORT's time is mostly GMC. The low person recall of best_grouped.pt is a real domain gap, not a bug. The oracle Work ID loss reflects real false re-links (131 of 141 re-links join different GT ids), made worse by the oracle feeding occluded and out-of-frame boxes.

defects.issue: The Work ID vs ByteTrack comparison has no control for probation, so the Work ID gains are overstated. '_uidonly' (mot17_eval.py:70-96) drops each new track's first 2 updates, but it is compared with raw ByteTrack that keeps them. Dropping those boxes on its own lowers IDSW and IDs/GT, because 1-2-frame fragments disappear. The 'workid_phase2' row with provisional ids (mot17_track.py:154-157) goes the other way: it adds about 1 ID per track (ids/gt 3.31 vs 1.69 for grouped).

defects.issue: Two fields in the run records are wrong. The workid run JSON's identity_kwargs is overwritten for each sequence, so it shows only the last sequence's frame-rate-dependent values. 'workers_created' is counted after consolidation.

confirmations: The detector P/R at conf > 0.35, IoU 0.5 is correct. My own recount with standard MOT17 distractor handling gives TP/FN/FP 22144/90153/2090 for grouped (R 19.72, P 91.38) and 48363/63934/5558 for coco (R 43.07, P 89.69). Both match the detections_conf035 CLEAR values exactly.

The detection cache is sound:
- The class column is all 3 for grouped and all 0 for coco.
- Minimum conf is 0.1000 or above, and every frame of every sequence is present.
- The busiest frame has 24 boxes (grouped) and 48 (coco), far below the max_det cap of 300.
- Rebuilding the predict path (letterbox, inference, single-label NMS, classes=[3]) reproduces the cached boxes on 214 of 214 sampled frames.

Class competition does not explain the low recall of best_grouped.pt. Multi-label NMS gives the same person recall as single-label (42.7% on sampled visible GT of 150 px or taller). No missed person has a box of another class with IoU >= 0.5 at conf > 0.35.

My TrackEval re-evaluation, written only to the scratchpad, reproduces the CSV values for 6 reference runs at both rates. All 28,187 (7 Hz) and 111,713 (native) oracle output boxes are exact GT boxes (0 unmatched).

The oracle ByteTrack native and 7 Hz MOT files regenerate byte-identically with the current mot17_track.py. The instrumented replays of oracle and coco Work ID reproduce the stored uid counts per sequence (oracle 48/59/94/18/54/42/60; coco live uids match workers_created + consolidation_merges).

TrackEval special-cases only MOT15 and MOT20 (mot_challenge_2d_box.py:326,360,391), so 'MOT17sub7' gets standard MOT17 pedestrian/distractor handling. No class-1 GT row has flag 0, and every distractor-class row has flag 0.

I found no errors in any frame or sequence:
- All 22 tracker logs and both eval runs exit 0.
- All runs contain the 7 sequences.
- TrackEval's duplicate-ID-per-frame check passed with BREAK_ON_ERROR on all 48 evaluated runs, including the offline remaps.
- Provisional ids (>= 1e6) never collide with uids.

The < 48 px no-embedding rule does not matter for the detector runs: 0 grouped boxes and 0.6% of coco boxes above 0.35 are under 48 px. In the oracle merges, only 5 of 243 merge pairs involve a GT identity with median height < 48 px.

In id_counts, Hungarian runs on raw IoU before the 0.5 cut, whereas CLEAR applies the cut first. The difference is immaterial: ids/gt changes by at most 0.011 and merged_ids by at most 1 on 5 runs checked.
BoT-SORT ran on ultralytics 8.4.75 in .venv-eval (lap 0.5.14 present) with frames passed, so GMC was active. boxmot is 26.0.0.
observations:
Grouped recall (19.7%) is a domain gap, not a bug.
- It depends strongly on size. For visible pedestrians (vis >= 0.5) by height band (<48, 48-75, 75-100, 100-150, 150-200, 200-300, >=300 px), grouped recall is 0.0/0.1/5.4/14.3/19.6/51.2/79.8% vs COCO 3.2/11.2/43.4/55.4/60.8/93.3/98.2%.
- It is not a pixel-resolution limit: at imgsz 1280 visible recall rises only from 30.2% to 32.2% on 107 sampled frames.
- grouped never detects 272 of the 546 GT identities in any frame (COCO misses 133).
- On MOT17-04, grouped detects 21.7% of visible pedestrians of 100 px or taller (COCO 65.0%); on MOT17-13 it detects 8.3% of all boxes.
- The overall COCO recall of 43% is mostly occlusion: 23.6% of GT boxes have visibility < 0.25 (49.4% in MOT17-02). For visible pedestrians of 100 px or taller, COCO recall is 65-97% per sequence.

The 0.35 filter, not association, decides the ranking against BoT-SORT. On the same input (feedall), ByteTrack ties or beats BoT-SORT with ReID and GMC: HOTA 24.68 vs 24.03 (grouped) and 41.03 vs 41.15 (coco). AssA is essentially equal (34.50 vs 34.28; 46.14 vs 46.34). BoT-SORT's lead over ByteTrack at 0.35 is DetA (16.98 vs 15.10; 36.94 vs 33.99). Its per-sequence gain is concentrated in MOT17-13 (moving camera; coco AssA 47.6 vs 40.2), and it is worse on MOT17-02, -04 and -11. By design its ReID can only rescue pairs with IoU >= 0.5 (proximity_thresh), so it is no long-range re-ID baseline.

StrongSORT and DeepOCSORT have low DetA because of their defaults: an effective min_conf of 0.6 for StrongSORT (the log line prints det_thresh=0.3, which is misleading) or det_thresh 0.5 for DeepOCSORT, plus min_hits/n_init 3. Their higher AssA (35.0/34.9 vs 34.3 grouped; 49.7/49.2 vs 46.9 coco) is computed on fewer, higher-confidence true positives, so it is partly a selection effect. The paper should quote min_conf 0.6, not 0.3.

The oracle Work ID losses are real identity errors. I replayed the run with instrumentation:
- The identity layer made 141 re-links; only 10 joined the same GT id.
- Of the 131 wrong ones: 45 jump at least 2 body heights, 8 link to a GT person who is still present, 10 are short-gap same-spot links (possible GT id fragmentation), and 68 are other cases.
- Similarity at decision has a median of 0.79 for wrong re-links vs 0.895 for correct ones.
- A visual check of 10 visible wrong re-links found at least 6 clearly different people, 1 that looks like the same person under a new GT id (MOT17-05 GT67 to GT83), and 3 undecidable.
- In MOT17-04, ByteTrack on oracle boxes is a perfect 83-to-83 match, so all 24 re-links there are wrong. Their median gap is 180 frames and median jump 3.2 body heights; for example, GT67 leaves at the top edge (y=-107, vis 0.01) at frame 519 and GT101 enters at the bottom edge at frame 618 under the same uid.
- End-of-session consolidation made 40 merges, 38 of them across GT identities, so '_offline' lowers AssA in every condition.

The oracle condition is extra hard for the histogram embedder. 23.6% of oracle boxes have visibility < 0.25 and 14.6% extend beyond the frame; no detector would produce such boxes. 68 of the 131 wrong re-links were decided on a box with visibility < 0.25, and 35 on a box clipped by the frame edge. On the static sequences (02, 04, 09) ByteTrack on oracle boxes has 0 IDSW, so the oracle mostly measures the false-link rate, not the benefit. A visibility-filtered oracle would be a fairer sensitivity check. On real coco detections the false-link rate is lower but still above half: of 319 re-links, 80 joined the same GT id, 139 a different one, and 100 could not be scored.

MOT17 GT itself splits some people into several ids. For example, MOT17-02 GT 14, 76, 77, 78, 79 and 80 sit at the same spot with 5-15-frame gaps and visibility near 0. The single oracle ByteTrack id that bridges them is counted in merged_ids, so merged_ids slightly overstates errors.

The 7 Hz combined numbers hide a collapse on moving-camera sequences.
- coco ByteTrack HOTA drops only 39.75 to 37.94 overall, but MOT17-13 goes 30.1 to 17.5 and MOT17-10 33.5 to 23.9, while the static sequences stay flat or improve.
- Even with oracle boxes, ByteTrack at 7 Hz scores HOTA 43.1 (MOT17-13) and 47.0 (MOT17-10), with IDSW 719 and 531. It keeps only 70.1% of the boxes in MOT17-13, because it has no camera-motion compensation and new tracks need 2 consecutive matches.
- The effective rates are 7.5 Hz (02, 04, 09, 10, 11), 7 Hz (05) and 6.25 Hz (13). The worst sequence is the slowest one.
- At 7 Hz, the probation drop costs much more: MOT17-13 oracle CLR_Re falls from 70.1% to 52.5% with uidonly.

COMBINED values are weighted by box count. MOT17-04 alone contributes 42.3% of GT boxes, and static sequences 63.6%, so the per-sequence and static/moving breakdown should accompany the combined numbers. The identity layer's harm concentrates in MOT17-05 (coco AssA 38.0 vs 45.1; oracle 72.3 vs 88.3).

The detections_conf035 rows in combined_metrics.csv have meaningless HOTA, AssA, IDF1, IDSW, MOTA and ids_per_gt values, because every detection is its own track. Only CLR_Re, CLR_Pr, TP, FP and FN are valid there.
The single CLR FP in the 7 Hz oracle run (MOT17-10) is not a frame-mapping bug: every output box is an exact GT box. It comes from CLEAR's continuity-preferring assignment and can be ignored.

verdict:
The runs are faithful to the brief and to the deployed code. Every run was reproduced on the cached inputs and matched the stored files exactly: the real SafetyPipeline with only its detector stubbed, the real ultralytics model.track, and default boxmot. There are no blocker or major defects. Three minor items:
(1) The Work ID runs use (f-1)/fps as clip time, not analyze.py's f/fps. Because of an exact-tie float comparison at the 3.0 s gate horizon, 3 of 56 Work ID sequence-runs change under analyze.py's time origin. Combined metrics move by at most 0.25 points; one sequence moves by up to 2.3 IDF1.
(2) CPU ms/frame was measured with unequal thread budgets and with two run streams going at once.
(3) The four oracle runs are not in run_partD.sh; their outputs reproduce exactly anyway.

observations:
Effective confidence thresholds differ widely even though the input is identical:
- StrongSORT keeps only conf ≥ 0.6 (boxmot trackers/strongsort/tracker.py:212).
- DeepOCSORT keeps only conf > 0.5 (deepocsort/tracker.py:145).
- BoT-SORT 8.4.75 can never match a box below 0.25: the low-score stage applies fuse_score and then a 0.5 threshold (ultralytics trackers/byte_tracker.py:419-422). It starts new tracks only at ≥ 0.25.
So relative to phase2's >0.35 feed, only BoT-SORT uses extra boxes (the 0.25-0.35 band); the boxmot trackers use fewer. The draft's statement that BoT-SORT and the boxmot trackers 'do see the low-confidence boxes' is true only at the input. This matters when interpreting the __feedall sensitivity runs.

Lost-track buffers differ by design. BoT-SORT keeps a lost track for 30 updates regardless of fps: 2.1 s at 14 fps (MOT17-05) and 1.2 s at 25 fps. boxmot uses max_age 30 frames. Phase2 ByteTrack keeps 1 s at every rate. Each is faithful to its tracker's defaults, but this should be stated in the comparison. Relatedly, run records list 'frame_rate_given' for BoT-SORT and boxmot (mot17_track.py:222, 253), although they never receive one.

- record['identity_kwargs'] is overwritten for each sequence (mot17_track.py:269). The native records therefore show only MOT17-13's fr=25 values (gate_horizon 75, coast_frames 12).
- The run JSONs do not record the supervision, ultralytics or boxmot versions (mot17_track.py:217).

The uid is decided and emitted on the 3rd evidence frame (identity.py:273-292), so a continuously visible new track has 2 provisional boxes. Provisional boxes per ByteTrack track: oracle native has 2 for 523 tracks, 1 for 23, 3 for 2 and 4 for 1; grouped native has 2 for 406, 1 for 58, 3 for 41, with up to 7 when there are gaps during probation.

- grouped: Person box tops sit a median 8.3 px above the GT top (mean 7.9; median offsets x1 +0.75, y1 -8.31, x2 -0.71, y2 +1.16).

This lowers DetA/LocA for the grouped detector independently of identity, and is part of the oracle-versus-detector gap.

Deployed-code fragility behind defect 1: IdentityManager._gap's strict dt_s > 3.0 decides gaps of exactly the horizon by float rounding. 42 frames at 14 fps, 90 at 30 fps and 75 at 25 fps all hit it. The comparison flips between the two time origins for about 8-11% of such frame pairs. With wall-clock time in live use this hardly matters. In clip evaluation it makes per-sequence Work ID numbers depend on the time origin.
